newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ growth falls to 2.6 pct in Mch yr-National Bank.
newsitem.headline: NZ growth falls to 2.6 pct in Mch yr-National Bank.

text.p: Economic growth in New Zealand eased to a five-year low of 2.6 percent in the year to March 1997, the National Bank said on Tuesday.
"For the first time since 1995 year-on-year growth simultaneously slowed in all fourteen regions," the Bank said in its Regional Trends report.
It said economic activity dropped 0.7 percent across New Zealand in the March quarter, representing the first quarterly decline since March 1991.
"Only four regions recorded a rise in activity in the quarter, the lowest number of regional economies to expand in a quarter since 1991," National Bank said.

It said business and consumer confidence dipped slightly in the March quarter, more prominently in the South Island with all of the southern regions showing a decline. Northland and Auckland were the only regions to record small rises in business confidence.
Consumer confidence was also weaker, with the Bay of Plenty recording the only rise in sentiment.
"Wellington recorded the largest drop in consumer confidence from its top ranking in the previous quarter, reinstating the gulf between Auckland and the rest of the country," the bank said.
Six regions recorded a rise in retail sales in the March quarter, led by the West Coast, Southland and Wellington.

"The official real seasonally adjusted series dipped 0.8 percent nationwide, wheras the series we use (which, due to data limitations, is the nominal retail trade figure deflated by its implicit deflator, and then seasonally adjusted) showed a 0.4 percent drop in the March quarter."
National Bank said the inter-island split revealed similar sized falls in both islands.
The South Island recorded a 4.8 percent rise in the value of residential building approvals over the quarter, while the North Island dropped 7.5 percent.
The value of commercial building consents recorded its second successive decline, with the South Island down 21 percent and the North Isand down 23 percent.
"Turnover in the national real estate market was virtually unchanged in March, with sales numbers dipping 0.2 percent in the quarter," National Bank said.
